newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - June 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - June 17.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Tuesday.
IRISH TIMES
- Double IRA killing of RUC men raises fear of loyalist backlash
- Bruton and Blair unite in scathing attack on Adams over IRA
killings
- EU leaders put single currency back on track
- Hewlett Packard in advanced talks over new Leixlip plant
- Norwich Union shares end first day trading at 325 pence
- Esat turns to CIE to get communications on line
- Mackie policy statement expected today
- Smurfit announces restructuring of senior management
IRISH INDEPENDENT
- IRA murder blows away the hope of peace
- Single currency back on track as EU leaders defuse a bitter
row over management
- Deputy prime minister Dick Spring rushes home to be with sick
son
- Ulster Bank see growth topping last year at 7.0 percent
- Dermot Smurfit heads up sales in Smurfit Group
- EMU deal threat to punt
THE EXAMINER
- Savage IRA killing of RUC men threatens wave of retaliation
- Single currency on launching pad after chaos is narrowly
averted
- If North tumbles into abyss, the Celtic Tiger will feel the
fall
- RUC death toll tops 300 as violence surges
